definitions.explanation: The number one. This is the most basic counting number in Japanese. When counting objects, いち is often combined with counters like {一|いっ}つ (hitotsu), {一|いっ}{個|こ} (ikko), or {一|いち}{人|にん} (ichinin), though the pronunciation may change depending on the counter.

examples.japanese: {一|いち}から{十|じゅう}まで{数|かぞ}えてください。
examples.english: Please count from one to ten.

examples.japanese: ペンを{一|いち}{本|ぽん}ください。
examples.notes: いち becomes いっ before ぽん

examples.japanese: {一|いち}{番|ばん}{好|す}きな{色|いろ}は{何|なん}ですか。
examples.english: What is your favorite (number one) color?

examples.japanese: {一|いち}{週間|しゅうかん}に{一|いち}{回|かい}、{友達|ともだち}と{近|ちか}くの{公園|こうえん}でサッカーをしています。
examples.english: Once a week, I play soccer with my friends at the park.

examples.japanese: {一|いち}{年|ねん}に{一|いち}{回|かい}、{家族|かぞく}みんなで{旅行|りょこう}に{行|い}くのが、うちの{楽|たの}しみなので、いつも{楽|たの}しみにしています。
examples.english: Going on a trip with the whole family once a year is our family's pleasure, so we always look forward to it.

notes:
{一|いち} is the number one. The reading changes depending on what follows it.

READING VARIATIONS:
- いち: standalone, before most counters ({一|いち}{人|にん}、{一|いち}{回|かい})
- いっ: before counters starting with k, s, t, p ({一|いっ}{個|こ}、{一|いっ}{冊|さつ}、{一|いっ}{杯|ぱい})
- ひと: native Japanese counting ({一|ひと}つ、{一|ひと}り)

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {一番|いちばん}: number one, the most
- {一度|いちど}: once
- {一緒|いっしょ}: together
- {一生|いっしょう}: one's whole life
- {一人|ひとり}: one person, alone

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {一|いち}から: from scratch, from the beginning
- {一|いち}か{八|ばち}か: all or nothing (idiom)
